title.narrative: National protection policies improved to extend coverage, enable social protection systems to be sustainable and provide adequate benefits, and support care work in line with international labour standards

description.narrative:
China’s 14th Five-Year Plan promotes innovation-based, coordinated, green, open, and shared development. The government, with social partners, aims to foster high-quality, job-rich economic growth, expand the multi-tier social security system, improve working conditions, especially for new forms of employment, and increase middle-income groups. These policies address demographic challenges (aging, low fertility, labor shortages), climate crisis transitions, and social protection disparities among workers and regions. Effective measures are needed to balance work and family responsibilities, with investment in the care economy to support public care services and infrastructure, particularly for women burdened with unpaid care work.
Through Country Outcome Programme CHN301, the ILO will support the government and social partners in building a universal, adequate, and sustainable multi-tier social security system. This support aims to extend social protection to vulnerable groups, ensure social insurance provides timely benefits, and benefit all Chinese citizens through a sustainable social protection system. The ILO collaborates with the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (MoHRSS) and social partners (All-China Federation of Trade Unions and China Enterprise Confederation) within the EU-China Project “Improving China’s Institutional Capacity towards Universal Social Protection” (Phase 2, 2023-2026), funded by the EU.
Additionally, the ILO supports tripartite constituents in promoting family-friendly policies and workplaces for workers with care responsibilities. A review of care policy in China is underway to identify gaps and develop recommendations for improving investment and services for workers with family responsibilities.
